chunks: Ali ibn Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn 'Imran al-Daqqaq (may Allah have mercy on him) said: Muhammad ibn Abi 'Abd Allah al-Kufi said: Musa ibn 'Imran, on the authority of his uncle al-Husayn ibn Yazid al-Nawfali, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Sufyan, said: Abu 'Ali al-Qassab related to me, saying: I was in the presence of Abu 'Abd Allah (peace be upon him). I said: 'All praise is to Allah, the limit of His Knowledge.' He said: 'Do not say that, for indeed, there is no limit to His Knowledge.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Sadiq say about the limit of Allah's knowledge?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) corrects a common theological misconception by rejecting the notion that divine knowledge is finite, thereby affirming the attribute of *La Nihaya* (no end). This correction underscores the Shia scholarly emphasis on distinguishing between created, limited knowledge and the uncreated, boundless knowledge of Allah, which encompasses all past, present, and future realities without exclusion. The brevity of the exchange highlights the precision required in describing divine attributes to avoid anthropomorphism or limitation.
